title: Architecture Reference
text:
The Codex version of the Clo-Author uses a split architecture:

a reusable home-local plugin
a lightweight project constitution inside each repository

That separation is the biggest architectural change from the Claude version.








Layer
Where It Lives
What It Does




Plugin manifest
home-local plugin
Registers the workflow with Codex


Skills
home-local plugin
Defines the 10 workflow entry points


Prompts
home-local plugin
Encodes worker, critic, referee, and orchestrator roles


References
home-local plugin
Supplies field, journal, and rubric knowledge


Hooks and scripts
home-local plugin
Detects projects, initializes repos, nudges review


Project constitution
repository AGENTS.md
Project-specific rules and expectations


Project marker
repository clo-author.toml
Activates the workflow for the repo


Durable evidence
repository quality_reports/
Stores specs, plans, logs, reviews, and scores

text:
Planning
Non-trivial work should be turned into a plan and saved to:

quality_reports/plans/

title: Architecture Reference
text:
Session reasoning

title: Architecture Reference
text:
Requirements and specs

title: User Guide
text:
You describe the research task in plain language or invoke one of the Clo-Author skills directly. Codex handles the rest through the plugin plus the project files in your repository.







You Do
The Workflow Does




Describe the task or name a skill
Picks the right workflow family


Approve or refine the plan when needed
Saves plans and logs to quality_reports/


Review important artifacts
Runs worker-critic or referee review by default


Decide when to ship
Applies the quality gates



For non-trivial work, the Codex version stays plan-first. For substantial artifacts, it defaults to a worker step and then a critic step.

title: User Guide
text:
new-project
Use this when you need a fresh repository scaffold.
What it does:

creates AGENTS.md
creates clo-author.toml
creates the research folder layout
creates quality_reports/ directories

Good prompt:
Use $new-project to initialize a new project on municipal bond markets.

title: User Guide
text:
discover
Use this for research interviews, literature review, data discovery, and broad ideation.
Typical outputs:

research specification
literature synthesis
data source memo
frontier map

Good prompt:
Use $discover to build a literature and data overview for the effect of rent control on mobility.

title: User Guide
text:
strategize
Use this for identification design, assumptions, robustness plans, and pre-analysis logic.
Typical outputs:

strategy memo
design options with trade-offs
robustness checklist
falsification plan

Good prompt:
Use $strategize to compare DiD and IV approaches for this project and recommend one.

title: User Guide
text:
analyze
Use this for data cleaning, estimation, robustness checks, figures, and tables.
Typical outputs:

scripts in scripts/
cleaned data artifacts
tables in paper/tables/
figures in paper/figures/

By default, substantial code and output changes should flow through worker-critic review.

title: User Guide
text:
write
Use this for paper drafting and revision.
Typical outputs:

introduction, data, strategy, results, conclusion
revision text
abstract and summary sections

The Codex version preserves the same writing standards: effect sizes, notation consistency, hedging control, and evidence-linked claims.

title: User Guide
text:
review
Use this for quality review, manuscript review, code review, or referee-style review.
Typical outputs:

worker-critic review report
manuscript issues list
code-quality report
journal-aware referee report

The same journal-aware review idea survives in the Codex version. The difference is invocation style, not review logic.

title: User Guide
text:
revise
Use this when you already have comments, findings, or referee reports and need to route them into action.
Typical outputs:

revision classification
response-letter draft
scoped follow-up tasks

title: User Guide
text:
talk
Use this to derive talks from the paper, audit an existing deck, or update presentation artifacts after paper changes.

title: User Guide
text:
submit
Use this when the project is nearing final packaging and you want replication, audit, and readiness checks.

title: User Guide
text:
tools
Use this for compile, validation, project-state inspection, and light housekeeping.

title: User Guide
text:
AGENTS.md
This is the Codex-facing project constitution. It tells the model how to behave in this repository and what the workflow expectations are.

title: User Guide
text:
clo-author.toml
This is the project marker. It lets the plugin detect the repository and load the Clo-Author workflow with the right defaults.

title: User Guide
text:
quality_reports/
This is where the workflow leaves evidence:

specs/
plans/
session_logs/
review and score artifacts

title: User Guide
text:
MEMORY.md
Use this for durable project-specific lessons, conventions, and corrections.

~/plugins/clo-author-codex exists
~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json contains clo-author-codex

text:
The project is not detected
Check:

paper/ exists
quality_reports/plans/ exists

python3 ~/plugins/clo-author-codex/scripts/detect_project.py <repo> returns MATCH

title: User Guide
section: Review is not happening when expected
text:
Review is not happening when expected
Check:

whether the change is substantial enough to trigger the workflow
whether the edit touched high-signal paths like paper/ or scripts/
whether the hook and queue scripts are present in the plugin

title: Skill Reference
text:
Quick Lookup








Skill
Use It For
Main Outputs




new-project
Initialize a new research repository
AGENTS.md, clo-author.toml, folder skeleton


discover
Interview, literature review, data discovery, ideation
discovery memos in quality_reports/


strategize
Identification strategy, design trade-offs, robustness plans
strategy memo


analyze
Scripts, estimation, tables, figures, cleaned data
scripts/, paper/tables/, paper/figures/


write
Drafting and revising paper sections
manuscript text and revision artifacts


review
Worker-critic review, code review, manuscript review, referee review
scored reports and quality decisions


revise
Turn comments into scoped follow-up work
response plans and revision tasks


talk
Generate or audit presentation artifacts
slides, audits, presentation updates


submit
Packaging, replication checks, final readiness
package artifacts and submission checks


tools
Compile, validate, inspect state, workflow housekeeping
utility output and verification evidence






new-project
Use when you want to initialize a fresh research repository.
Example:
Use $new-project to initialize a new project on hospital mergers.
Expected outcome:

project scaffold
AGENTS.md
clo-author.toml
quality_reports/ directories




discover
Use when you need to understand a question, map literature, or identify data sources.
Example:
Use $discover to build a literature and data overview for cash transfers and labor supply.
Typical modes in practice:

interview-driven discovery
literature review
data discovery
broad ideation




strategize
Use when the task is about identification, assumptions, robustness, falsification, or design comparison.
Example:
Use $strategize to compare staggered DiD and event-study options for this setting.
Expected outcome:

strategy memo
design recommendation
assumption checklist
robustness and falsification plan




analyze
Use when implementing analysis code or reviewing analysis outputs.
Example:
Use $analyze to implement the baseline specification and generate the first results table.
Expected outcome:

scripts in scripts/
outputs in paper/tables/ and paper/figures/
verification evidence

Substantial analysis work should trigger worker-critic review by default.



write
Use when drafting or revising paper text.
Example:
Use $write to draft the introduction and a clean contribution paragraph.
Expected outcome:

manuscript sections
revised text
writing review findings where needed




review
Use for quality review, referee-style review, or pre-submission pressure testing.
Example:
Use $review to run a methods-heavy review on paper/main.tex.
Expected outcome:

code or manuscript review report
critic findings
referee-style findings
quality-gate recommendation

Common review patterns:

manuscript review
code review
methods-focused review
journal-aware referee review




revise
Use when you already have findings and want to convert them into a response plan.
Example:
Use $revise to classify this referee report and route the follow-up work.
Expected outcome:

issue classification
response plan
revised-task routing




talk
Use when building or auditing slides derived from the paper.
Example:
Use $talk to turn the current draft into a 15-minute seminar deck.
Expected outcome:

slide deck or talk outline
talk audit
updated presentation assets




submit
Use when checking whether the project is ready to ship.
Example:
Use $submit to audit the replication package and tell me what still blocks submission.
Expected outcome:

packaging checklist
replication audit
readiness summary




tools
Use for small but workflow-critical tasks such as compilation, validation, and state inspection.
Example:
Use $tools to compile the paper and summarize any LaTeX issues.
Expected outcome:

compile result
validation output
context or state summary




Invocation Style
The Codex version supports two practical ways of working:

Natural language request:

Build a literature review on local public finance and save it under quality_reports.

Explicit skill naming:

Use $discover to build a literature review on local public finance.
Natural language is the default. Explicit skill naming is the sharper tool when you want to force a specific workflow family.

title: Customization Guide
text:
Overview
The Codex version of the Clo-Author is split between a reusable home-local plugin and lightweight files inside each project repository.








Layer
Location
Purpose




Project constitution
AGENTS.md
Repository-specific workflow rules


Project marker
clo-author.toml
Project detection and workflow defaults


Durable memory
MEMORY.md
Reusable project learnings


Skills
home-local plugin skills/
Workflow entry points


Prompts
home-local plugin prompts/
Worker, critic, referee, and orchestration roles


References
home-local plugin references/
Domain, journal, and rubric material


Hooks and scripts
home-local plugin hooks.json, hooks/, scripts/
Detection, nudges, initialization, migration, logging



This keeps the repository small while making the reusable workflow portable across projects.



AGENTS.md
AGENTS.md is now the project constitution. It is the repository-level entry point that tells Codex:

what this project is
which workflow norms apply
where outputs belong
how strict the review and verification rules should be

Keep it short and practical. It should guide the workflow, not become an encyclopedia.



clo-author.toml
clo-author.toml is the project marker that allows the plugin to recognize the repository.
Typical contents:

project name
slug
field
institution
workflow defaults
quality thresholds

When the plugin sees clo-author.toml plus the expected directory structure, it can treat the repository as a Clo-Author project.



Skills
The Codex version keeps the same 10 workflow families, but presents them as skills and natural-language workflows.
The plugin skill directories are:

new-project
discover
strategize
analyze
write
review
revise
talk
submit
tools

You can customize a skill in two ways:

update the skill summary and workflow instructions
update the prompt and reference files the skill relies on




Prompts and Role Design
The old Claude version used an explicit .claude/agents/ registry. The Codex version keeps the same conceptual roles, but treats them as prompt roles and workflow roles:

workers
critics
referees
orchestrator
verifier

The current plugin also preserves the old agent texts under prompts/legacy-agents/ so migration remains traceable.
Use prompt-layer customization when you want to change:

tone of reviews
strictness of scoring
field-specific reasoning style
submission or referee behavior




References
Field adaptation still lives in reference material.
Key reference areas:

domain profile
journal profiles
quality rules
legacy rules and legacy skill materials

Use references when you want to change:

field conventions
preferred journals
common data sources
typical identification strategies
review culture




Hooks and Scripts
The Codex version uses plugin hooks and helper scripts instead of the old repository-local hook configuration.
Current responsibilities include:

detecting Clo-Author repositories
nudging post-edit review
initializing projects
migrating old repositories
writing session-log stubs

Keep hooks lightweight. Use scripts for mechanical actions and keep nuanced reasoning in the workflow itself.



Template Assets
The plugin ships a project template that can generate:

AGENTS.md
MEMORY.md
clo-author.toml
research directories
quality_reports/ scaffolding

Customize the template when you want every new repository to inherit a different default structure.



Domain and Journal Customization
The research logic is still highly field-sensitive.
Customize:

domain profiles for field norms and data sources
journal profiles for review culture and contribution bar
manuscript and analysis conventions in AGENTS.md

That combination usually matters more than changing the skills themselves.



Migration-Aware Customization
If you are still running legacy .claude/ assets alongside the plugin:

keep the old assets intact during the first migration pass
move new customization into the Codex-facing layers
use the migration appendix to keep the mapping clear

See Migration from Claude for the exact correspondence table.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
The Codex version of the Clo-Author keeps the same role design as the Claude version, but the runtime interpretation is different.
Instead of depending on a Claude-only agent registry, Codex uses:

skill-level workflow entry points
prompt roles for workers, critics, and referees
hooks and scripts for automatic nudges
saved reports and logs as the durable audit trail

The important thing that stayed the same is the separation of powers: creators create, critics review, referees pressure-test, and infrastructure coordinates.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
Librarian
Collects and synthesizes literature, maps the frontier, and positions the project in the conversation.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
librarian-critic
Checks for missing literatures, recency gaps, and skewed coverage.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
Explorer
Searches for datasets, evaluates feasibility, and links data options to the research design.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
explorer-critic
Checks measurement validity, sample fit, and identification compatibility.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
Strategist
Designs the empirical strategy, assumptions, falsification tests, and robustness plan.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
strategist-critic
Stress-tests the identification logic, inference, and credibility of the design.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
Data-engineer
Handles data cleaning, variable construction, merges, and output-ready intermediate assets.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
Coder
Implements the main analysis, robustness checks, and result-producing scripts.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
coder-critic
Reviews reproducibility, strategy alignment, and code quality.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
Writer
Drafts or revises manuscript sections, preserving notation, evidence alignment, and empirical-paper structure.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
writer-critic
Checks claims, notation, LaTeX quality, and whether the prose outruns the evidence.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
Editor
Screens the paper, frames the review route, and synthesizes final editorial-style decisions.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
domain-referee
Reviews contribution, literature positioning, and substantive relevance.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
methods-referee
Reviews identification, estimation, inference, and robustness.
These roles remain especially useful near submission or major revision milestones.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
Storyteller
Builds talk structures and presentation artifacts from the paper.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
storyteller-critic
Checks slide narrative, readability, and fidelity to the paper.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
Verifier
Confirms whether compilation, packaging, and artifact-level checks actually pass.

title: Agents and Roles
text:
Orchestrator
Coordinates the broader workflow: planning, routing, review pressure, and quality-gate logic.

title: The Clo-Author Codex
text:
The Clo-Author is a Codex-first workflow for empirical social science research. It preserves the original clo-author ideas — structured planning, worker-critic review, journal-aware peer review, and quality gates — but moves the runtime into a home-local Codex plugin plus a lightweight project constitution inside each repository.
Historical origin: Pedro Sant’Anna’s claude-code-my-workflow, reoriented for empirical research publication.

title: The Clo-Author Codex
text:
Get Started in 5 Minutes

Step 1: Prepare the local plugin
The recommended runtime is a home-local plugin:

plugin root: ~/plugins/clo-author-codex
marketplace entry: ~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json

The plugin carries the reusable parts of the workflow: skills, prompts, references, hooks, scripts, and template assets.


Step 2: Clone or open a project
gh repo fork hugosantanna/clo-author --clone
cd clo-author
If you already have a repository, make sure it has AGENTS.md, clo-author.toml, and the standard research directories so the plugin can detect it automatically.


Step 3: Open the repository in Codex
Once inside Codex, the plugin should detect the project and load the Clo-Author workflow through:

AGENTS.md
clo-author.toml
the repository layout



Step 4: Start with a skill or plain-language request
Examples:

“Use $discover to build a literature review on health insurance and labor supply.”
“Use $review to run a methods-heavy review on paper/main.tex.”
“Use $new-project to initialize a new empirical project on municipal finance.”

Natural language works too. The explicit skill names are useful when you want to steer Codex directly.

title: The Clo-Author Codex
text:
What Happens Behind the Scenes
The Codex version keeps the same workflow logic:

plan first for substantial work
save artifacts to quality_reports/
run worker-critic review by default
route to referee-style review when needed
verify before completion

The main difference is the runtime model. Instead of a Claude-only command stack, Codex uses:

plugin skills
prompt roles
project detection hooks
helper scripts for initialization, migration, logging, and review nudges

title: The Clo-Author Codex
text:
Day 1 Checklist

Ensure the home-local plugin is installed
Open a repository with AGENTS.md and clo-author.toml
Confirm Codex detects the project
Start with $discover, $review, or $new-project
Review the generated plan or artifact
Let the worker-critic loop run before treating the result as final

That is the core loop. Everything else — prompts, references, hooks, and reports — supports that workflow.

text:
Where to Go Next

title: Migration from Claude
text:
The Codex version is a migration, not a reinvention. Most of the research logic stayed the same:

plan first
save artifacts to disk
use worker-critic review
keep referee-style pressure testing
gate important work with quality thresholds

What changed is the runtime architecture.

title: Migration from Claude
text:
1. The project entry file
The old version started with CLAUDE.md. The new version starts with:

AGENTS.md
clo-author.toml

AGENTS.md tells Codex how to behave in the repository. clo-author.toml tells the plugin that the repository belongs to the Clo-Author workflow.

title: Migration from Claude
text:
2. The reusable infrastructure
The old version copied most infrastructure into every repository. The new version moves reusable parts into the home-local plugin:

skills
prompts
references
hooks
scripts
template assets

title: Migration from Claude
text:
3. The invocation style
The old version emphasized slash commands. The new version emphasizes:

plain-language workflow requests
explicit skill naming when useful

Examples:
Use $discover to run a literature review.
Use $review to run a methods-focused manuscript review.
Use $new-project to scaffold a new repository.

title: Migration from Claude
text:
4. The automation model
The old version depended on Claude-specific hooks and command routing. The new version uses plugin hooks and scripts for:

project detection
project initialization
migration
post-edit review nudges

title: Migration from Claude
text:
For an existing repository

Keep the legacy .claude/ assets in place during the first migration pass.
Add AGENTS.md.
Add clo-author.toml.
Confirm the plugin detects the repository.
Start using skills or natural-language Codex requests.
Migrate customization into the Codex-facing layers over time.

title: Migration from Claude
text:
For a new repository

Install the home-local plugin.
Use new-project to scaffold the repository.
Fill in AGENTS.md and clo-author.toml.
Customize field and journal references.

title: Migration from Claude
text:
Keep these

paper/
data/
scripts/
quality_reports/
explorations/
bibliography and supporting documents

title: Migration from Claude
text:
Add these

AGENTS.md
clo-author.toml
Codex-oriented plans, specs, and logs if they are missing

title: Migration from Claude
text:
Do not delete too early

legacy .claude/ assets
old quality reports
old references or journal profiles

The first safe milestone is coexistence. Hard cutover can happen later.

title: Migration from Claude
section: Is the Claude version still supported?
text:
Is the Claude version still supported?
This documentation set is now Codex-first. The old materials can still exist in the repository for migration traceability, but the active guidance has moved to Codex.

title: Migration from Claude
section: Do I still have the same agent roles?
text:
Do I still have the same agent roles?
Yes, conceptually. They now live as prompt roles and workflow roles rather than a Claude-only runtime registry.

title: Migration from Claude
section: Do I lose the peer-review system?
text:
Do I lose the peer-review system?
No. The Codex version keeps the same editor, referee, and quality-gate concepts.

title: Migration from Claude
section: Is the new version less automatic?
text:
Is the new version less automatic?
No. The goal is still strong automation, but the mechanism is now plugin-driven instead of Claude-specific.
